title: Korean healthcare data residency
reference: Everything stays in the Seoul region; disaster recovery uses zones and backups inside Seoul, not another country.

turns.ask: We are building a patient appointment booking web app for a clinic in South Korea. By law all health records must never leave Korea. Please design the architecture with a database.
We also need disaster recovery so the system stays up if something fails.
Doctors will upload MRI and CT scans. Add object storage for those files.

title: Serverless ticketing API scaling
reference: SAE autoscaling is expressed in the existing SAE node (no Auto Scaling node), perhaps read replicas or a bigger cache.

turns.ask: I need a concert ticketing API built on SAE because we have zero ops engineers. Include a relational database and a cache layer.
Ticket sales open tomorrow and we expect 20x our normal traffic. Make sure everything scales automatically to handle the spike.

title: Auto Scaling for ECS website
reference: Auto Scaling attached to the ECS servers (this is the correct use of Auto Scaling).

turns.ask: Set up a small company website using two ECS instances and an RDS database in Singapore.
Our visitor count doubles every weekend. I want the servers to scale out and back in automatically based on load.

title: Budget blog with high availability
reference: Two zones for the app and database where affordable, a clear note about the cost effect, no heavy services.

turns.ask: I run a local newspaper blog. Our monthly cloud budget is $150 max. Design something that fits.
Readers want to leave comments. Add a comment system backed by a database.
We had an outage last week that took us offline for hours. Please make it more resilient without blowing up our costs.

title: AI agent for office team
reference: A ready-made assistant (QwenWork for office staff, Qoder Teams for developers) and one short question about who the team is.

turns.ask: I want to roll out an AI coding agent to everyone at my office. We work together daily but I'm not sure which plan fits best.

title: Swap OpenSearch for Elasticsearch (Korean)
reference: Swaps the product on the existing search node, nothing else changes; say and why text in Korean.

turns.ask: 상품 검색을 OpenSearch 대신 Elasticsearch로 바꿔주세요.

title: Swap RocketMQ for Kafka (Chinese)
reference: Swaps the product on the existing queue node; say and why text in Chinese.

turns.ask: 请把订单消息队列从RocketMQ换成Kafka。

title: Closed Mumbai region for mobile game
reference: Says Mumbai is closed, draws the stack in Singapore with edge acceleration (ESA, CDN or Global Accelerator).

turns.ask: We're launching a multiplayer mobile game for Indian players. Put the game servers in Mumbai so latency is as low as possible.

title: Qwen models for Cline users
reference: Token Plan with per-member keys (the team plan for tools they already use), not Qoder and not Coding Plan.

turns.ask: My 12 developers all code in VS Code using the Cline extension. We want to plug Qwen models into it with a predictable fixed cost per developer each month.

title: DDoS protection for game login API
reference: An edge layer with DDoS protection in front of the load balancer or gateway, then the login service across two zones with a cache and database.

turns.ask: Our online game's login API keeps getting hammered by massive DDoS attacks. Design the full protection layer and the backend service behind it.
